bug_semantics: Stored graph-configuration XSS. An authenticated low-privilege user could POST a config_json object containing a style such as mispStyles.Event.svgIcon. The save route checked only that the string parsed as JSON and persisted the complete object; the list route returned the stored string unchanged. When a viewer with access to the saved row (notably an administrator, because administrators list every user's configs) loaded it, graphConfigModal.js parsed config_json and applyConfig() spread every property of each stixStyles/mispStyles entry into GRAPH_CONFIG. A subsequent graph render passed that style map to Pivotick as nodeStyleMap. The bundled Pivotick renderer treats svgIcon as markup (both a template path using template.innerHTML = i.svgIcon.trim() and node rendering using an SVG element's innerHTML), so a crafted SVG event handler executes in the viewer's browser. Loading/applying the saved configuration is the victim interaction.
flaw_origin: Commit a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a is the atomic first writer of the vulnerable cross-user path. It added the GraphConfig table/model, /graph_config/save and /graph_config/list, the saved-config modal/load code, and applyConfig(), whose unrestricted object spread copied attacker-controlled style members such as svgIcon into GRAPH_CONFIG. The pre-existing parent already rendered trusted built-in styles with Pivotick, but had no saved-config file, persistence route, load path, or applyConfig bridge from another user's stored JSON to that renderer.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a` shows author and committer `ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>` and only the subject `add: [config] edit/create a json config for graph`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, bot identity, or other explicit AI attribution.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j8cv-pjx7-pvqf identifies CVE-2026-73158, describes saved graph config style properties reaching Pivotick's HTML-interpreted svgIcon, and directly references commit 9b317587fa4ec11b6f72c2d1d8b98a686537b4fb; its package version fields are Unknown. BIC search: in the validated full-history clone, `git log --all --reverse -S'graph_config/save' -- website/web/convert/convert.py website/web/static/js/graph/graphConfigModal.js` first returns a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a (the later 672ca701b3933d930470a7688c86f979c0900bf8 is only a rename). `git log --reverse -L '/export function applyConfig/,+24:website/web/static/js/graph/convertGraph.js' a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a` likewise shows that a0a9834 first added applyConfig and the exact unrestricted statements `GRAPH_CONFIG.stixStyles[k] = { ...(GRAPH_CONFIG.stixStyles[k] ?? {}), ...v }` and the equivalent mispStyles spread. `git show --format=fuller a0a9834... -- website/web/convert/convert.py website/web/convert/convert_core.py website/web/static/js/graph/convertGraph.js website/web/static/js/graph/graphConfigModal.js website/db_class/db.py` shows the same commit adding: JSON-parse-only validation before save; raw config_json persistence and list serialization; `_loadConfig` doing `JSON.parse(cfg.config_json)` then `applyConfig(patch)`; and the new graph-config schema/model. Sink/data flow: at the BIC tree, convertGraph.js lines 437-445 select GRAPH_CONFIG.mispStyles/stixStyles and pass it to `new window.Pivotick(... render: { nodeStyleMap: styleMap ... })`. Extracting the `svgIcon` contexts from `git show a0a9834...:website/web/static/js/pivotick.umd.js` shows Pivotick's icon helper doing `const e=document.createElement("template"); e.innerHTML=i.svgIcon.trim()` and its generic node renderer doing `const l=document.createElementNS(...,"svg"); l.innerHTML=e.svgIcon`. Parent absence: `git cat-file -e 11b0bc4583022cd863244af07040fcf5d9405738:website/web/static/js/graph/graphConfigModal.js` fails because the file is absent; the a0a9834 parent-to-child diff adds graph_config_save/list and applyConfig as new functions, so the parent has neither the persistence/load source nor the unsafe merge. The BIC is a normal one-parent commit (parent 11b0bc4583022cd863244af07040fcf5d9405738), not a merge, move, revert, release commit, or reconstructed squash aggregate. Fix: `git show --format=fuller 9b317587fa4ec11b6f72c2d1d8b98a686537b4fb` shows the direct advisory fix adding strict server-side validate_graph_config on save, sanitize_stored_graph_config on list for legacy rows, client sanitizeConfigPatch before every applyConfig merge, and allowing style entries only shape/color/size (therefore dropping svgIcon and iconClass). Release boundary: `git rev-parse v1.2^{} v1.3^{} v1.4^{} v1.5^{}` resolves respectively to 8097afb2908eb292c30bfda94648631a781e38af, ecd04d494b0fda2ab39fb56472785388c2d5872e, bc46b6ed186786e672c1229d014a6d0a448fedad, and fe093f9a1f9727068bc7e82ba47630907d859edb. `git tag --contains a0a9834...` returns v1.3, v1.4, v1.5, while `git tag --contains 9b317587...` returns only v1.5. Blob checks corroborate this: `git grep` finds the unrestricted mispStyles spread at line 569 in both v1.3 and v1.4, finds no graph_config/save in v1.2, and finds `patch = sanitizeConfigPatch(patch)` plus server validate/sanitize calls in v1.5. Thus repository tags v1.3 and v1.4 are vulnerable, v1.2 predates the feature, and v1.5 is the first fixed tag.
reasoning: The vulnerable primitive in Pivotick existed as a sink for trusted styles before the saved-config feature, but that alone was not exploitable through this advisory's cross-user route. The smallest true BIC is therefore the single feature commit that simultaneously made arbitrary nested styles persistable/retrievable and copied their unknown properties into the style map consumed by Pivotick. Both -S and -L history converge on a0a9834, its immediate parent directly lacks the source/bridge, and later renames are not introducers. The advisory's referenced 9b317587 commit directly closes all three lifecycle points (new saves, legacy rows on list, and browser application) and first ships in v1.5. AI judgment is restricted to the raw BIC commit object: it has a human author/committer identity and no explicit AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any signals on later commits or the fix.
